title: Epoch-based manifest erasure coordinator with CDN cache invalidation
creator: Sasha Patel
description:
Problem: Console usage events and derived analytics are material to customer support and product metrics, but we need a robust, auditable erase flow for PII that: 1) supports streaming ingestion and incremental backfills; 2) produces tamper-evident deletion proofs for audits; 3) invalidates cached analytic artifacts (CDN/edge dashboards) that may contain retained PII; and 4) operates without large snapshotting backfills that increase cost and blast radius.

Proposal: implement an Epoch Manifest Erasure Coordinator (EMEC) that orchestrates deletion across ingestion, store, transforms, and CDN cache. The coordinator will: create signed epoch manifests that list erased record identifiers (IDs and hashed keys), push manifests to downstream processors, produce a cryptographic deletion attestation per epoch, and issue CDN edge invalidation tokens tied to manifest proofs. The manifest approach allows incremental, idempotent deletions and efficient backfills: processors consume manifests to reconcile state and emit compensating deletes instead of full-table scans.

Key components:
- Manifest format: compact, schema-versioned JSONL with stable record identifiers and a per-epoch signature (Ed25519). Manifests include source, epoch_id, deletion_range, proof_public_key_version.
- Coordinator API: REST endpoints to create epoch manifests, check status, retrieve attestation, and mark manifests as "sealed" for audit retention.
- Downstream consumers: streaming transformers (Beam/Flink) will subscribe to manifest topics and apply deletes in-place or emit compensating tombstones to Kafka topics that storage services consume.
- CDN invalidation: Coordinator will mint short-lived CDN invalidation tokens that reference manifest signature. Edge dashboards will verify token+manifest and evict or mark cached tiles as stale. For CDNs without proof verification, the coordinator will trigger targeted purge requests using CDN APIs (with rate limits).
- Audit artifacts: Each sealed manifest will produce an immutable deletion attestation (signed statement + manifest URL) stored in the privacy-archive S3 bucket with retention per customer policy. These will be exportable to customers and legal teams.
- Safe-delete window: a configurable hold window (default 24h) between manifest creation and sealed attestation to allow replay/backpressure handling; manifests may be retried/appended prior to sealing.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Using signatures and immutable manifests increases storage of small files but simplifies proofs and prevents accidental replays.
- Targeted CDN purges are not guaranteed to reach every edge (varies by CDN). Token-based eviction with verification is preferred but requires edge code changes (console SDK).
- Backfill efficiency depends on downstream consumer implementation; we will provide a reference Flink consumer that applies deletes without full scan.
- Legal holds: manifests can be marked as "hold" which prevents sealing and attestation; legal-hold flow will be delegated to compliance team APIs.

Risks/mitigations:
- Risk: high throughput manifests overwhelm downstream processors. Mitigation: shard manifests by customer and use consumer group autoscaling; provide batching and rate-limit knobs.
- Risk: CDN token adoption lag. Mitigation: fallback to CDN API purge and monitor success rates; include a metrics dashboard.

Deliverables:
- API spec and OpenAPI file for EMEC endpoints (link below)
- Manifest schema v1 and reference generator library (Go/Python)
- Flink consumer reference implementation + unit/integration tests
- Edge SDK token verifier (console JS) and CDN purge adapter
- Attestation storage and export endpoint

Success metrics:
- 95% of deletion manifests are processed end-to-end within 30 minutes under normal load
- CDN cache eviction success >= 90% for supported CDNs within 2 hours
- Audit export generation time < 5 minutes for a single sealed epoch
acceptance_criteria: EMEC API deployed to staging with OpenAPI spec and auth guard
Manifest v1 published and generator library available in mono-repo
Reference Flink consumer processes manifests and applies deletes in integration test (no full-table scans)
Attestation files are signed and stored in privacy-archive with correct retention metadata
Console edge SDK verifies tokens and marks affected dashboard tiles stale; fallback purge path exercised in integration tests
Monitoring dashboard emits metrics for manifest processing latency, CDN purge success rate, and attestation generation time
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Infra, Analytics, Compliance. Decided to prefer manifest signatures over centralized index to simplify audits (Sasha).
2026-02-22: Architecture review - Security requested HSM-backed signing for attestation keys. Action: coordinate with Security for KMS/HSM requirement (assigned to Miguel).
2026-02-28: Draft OpenAPI posted: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRIV/EMEC+-+API (doc link). Asked for feedback from Analytics team on consumer contract.
2026-03-03: Spike complete for manifest generator in Go; generator supports streaming output to Kafka topic 'privacy.manifests.v1'. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8934 (WIP).

2026-03-06: Flink consumer prototype can apply deletes in local integration using test fixtures (no production data). Noted edge-case: duplicate manifest entries must be idempotent; fixed by using delete-with-version semantics.
2026-03-09: Security review scheduled; created ticket ENG-140009 to integrate signing with KMS. Adding tests for key rotation and signature verification in CI.
2026-03-10: Began work on CDN purge adapter. Need confirmation from Growth on supported CDN providers and API limits. Added label 'cdn-invalidation' to surface to Growth/Platform teams.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Staging: Deploy EMEC service, generator, and reference consumer to staging. Run synthetic manifests against staging CDN shim.
Phase 2 - Canary: Enable per-customer manifest generation for <5% of traffic. Monitor manifest processing latency and purge success. Disable on regressions.
Phase 3 - Gradual: Expand to 50% and then 100% once SLAs stable. Turn on attestation export to privacy-archive.
Phase 4 - Retro: Run compliance export exercises with Legal and Customer Success; collect feedback and iterate.
